tools.name: find_animation_titles
tools.description: Find animated SERIES and FILMS (animation library only — mostly anime, plus Western animation) that fit what the user is making — by a story brief in plain words ("a quiet coming-of-age story about two sisters in a seaside town, bittersweet, summer"), by a title it should be like (like: "Akira"), by a LOOK (an image or frame ids — titles whose frames look like it), and/or by genre, theme, style, studio, movie/series and year. Signals combine. Returns each title with studio, director, genres, themes, its look, a synopsis, a poster, and for a look search the frames that matched.

brief.description: The story, premise, mood or world in plain words

like.description: A title (name or slug) the results should be like in story

image.description: An image URL or data: URL — titles that look like it

title.description: Only inside this series / film (slug or name)

tools.name: find_by_craft
tools.description: Find frames by specific cinematography craft attributes — lens character, shot size, visual style, setting, time of day, director, or year range. All optional; combine to narrow. Use this to refine a search precisely.

tools.name: find_similar
tools.description: Find frames visually/semantically similar to a given frame id (from a prior result). Use this to pull more references like one the user shortlisted.

tools.name: get_animation_sequence
tools.description: A frame in its sequence: the shots just before and after it in the same episode / film, in order, each with its still and caption — to see how a moment is built, or to lay a beat out across several canvas panels. With clips: true, each shot's clip plus the continuous "run" video that covers them (run_url, with from/to seconds).

frame_id.description: A frame id from earlier results (or "slug:label")

clips.description: true = also return each frame's clip and sequence videos (1 credit per video on top of the call). Ask only when the user wants to see it move.

tools.name: get_animation_title
tools.description: One anime series or film in depth, by slug or name: synopsis, studio and key credits, main characters, genres, themes, its look, the trailer, how many shots are indexed, titles with a similar look and a similar story, and sample frames spread across it (frames: 0–24, default 6).

title.description: Slug or name, e.g. "akira-1988" or "Your Name"

clips.description: true = also return each frame's clip and sequence videos (1 credit per video on top of the call). Ask only when the user wants to see it move.

tools.name: get_commercial
tools.description: The full breakdown of one commercial by id: idea, logline, tagline, product, audience, every credit by role (director, agency, production company, DP, editor, music, post, sound, VFX), every award (show, year, level, category), craft numbers (shots, average shot length, cuts per minute, when the product / brand / emotional peak / end card land), the script with timings, and the shot list (caption, tags and still per shot; with clips: true, each shot's clip too).

stills.description: Include each shot's still image (1 credit per shot). Leave off unless the user wants to see the shots.

clips.description: true = also return a short clip of each shot (1 credit per clip on top of the call). Ask only when the user wants to see the shots move.

tools.name: get_frame_details
tools.description: Get the full metadata, a preview image and the FrameThrower link for a single frame id. For the full-resolution file or the depth map (camera geometry for image generation), call get_frame_image.

tools.name: get_frame_image
tools.description: One frame's image at a paid size, as a link valid for an hour: "full" = the original full-resolution file (5 credits), "large" = 1280px (2), "depth" = the precomputed depth map, ControlNet-ready (2). Search results show a preview only — use this when the user wants the actual image for a deck, document, download or an image-generation pipeline.

tools.name: search_animation_frames
tools.description: Find frames in FrameThrower's ANIMATION library — animated series and films only, never live-action (mostly anime, plus Western animation; the whole of every title, not a sample) for a scene, a moment or a CHARACTER LOOK, described in plain words: "a girl on a rooftop at dusk watching the city lights", "two kids running through a summer field", "a tall man with a scarred face and a long black coat, rain". Narrow by title, genre, theme, style (80s cel, watercolour, neon night…), studio, movie/series and year. Each frame has a caption of what is in it, a 640px still for looking at, the full-size still, the frame id and a link. At most 3 frames per title unless per_title says otherwise.
